title: A global perspective on adaptive radiation: advances, issues, and future directions
content: Adaptive radiation—the evolutionary divergence of members of a single phylogenetic lineage into a variety of different adaptive forms (Futuyma 1998)—is widely considered responsible for generating much of Earth’s remarkable diversity (Simpson 1953, Gillespie 2024). Although a unified definition of ‘adaptive radiation’ has attracted much debate in the literature (Olson and Arroyo-Santos 2009, Glor 2010, Givnish 2015), the general process is, and has been, of great interest to evolutionary biologists throughout the history of the field.
